svg.aria-label: A long graduated measuring edge lies across a paper-cream page in ink line only. Its left span carries evenly paced graduations; its middle span runs on as a bare line with no graduations at all, bracketed beneath by a dashed span; its right span resumes with graduations at twice the pitch and then the edge simply stops, capped and cut. Set apart to the right, with an empty gap between them and no line joining the two, a second shorter edge is turned a few degrees out of true and carries six graduations hanging below it instead of standing above, with two separate short strokes set further apart again. One kiln-orange mark, the only warm mark on the page, has come away from the first edge at the point where its graduations resume and lies below it, slightly adrift.
svg.title: The Still · England — the span with no graduations, and the edge that does not join
svg.desc:
A composition for the England piece. Paper-cream ground, pure line, no fills, tone carried by stroke opacity alone.
The object is the regulator's own instrument, drawn once. Its left span is graduated and in use. Its middle span is drawn as a continuous line with NO graduations: the eight years in which the best-graded schools were not routinely inspected, which is a span of time that was still running and still being reported on while nothing in it was being measured. The dashed bracket beneath that span marks it as a span rather than as a gap in the drawing. The right span resumes at twice the pitch — the regulator went back in and inspected a great many of them in one year — and then the edge stops, capped: the overall grade stopped being awarded.
The second edge is a DIFFERENT instrument and the composition refuses to join them. It is turned out of true, its six graduations hang below its line rather than standing above it, and two further strokes sit apart from the six. Nothing connects it to the first edge and the gap between them is empty, because the regulator has said in writing that the new grades cannot be compared to the old ones. Six graduations because the renewed framework grades six core evaluation areas; two separate strokes because safeguarding is reported apart from them, as met or not met.
The one kiln-orange mark is a single graduation that has come away from the first edge at the point where measurement resumed, lying below the line and slightly adrift. It is a pointer at a sentence in the body and carries NO magnitude.
NOTHING IN THIS STILL ENCODES A PROPORTION. The graduation pitches are set by the pen and not by any published figure; the two spans are not to scale against each other; neither edge is a scale of grades and no mark stands for a percentage. The piece's own first guardrail is that there is no composite of the two rulers and the piece may not build one — a still whose proportions encoded either distribution would be a chart of it, and a still that set the two edges on one axis would be the composite the Editor refused.
